items.prompt: White is thinking about the pawn move c5. Predict, then check: after it, will the bishop on d3 attack more squares than it does now? (Count only squares not held by its own pieces.)
hints: Find the piece the question names and count the squares it attacks now, skipping squares its own pieces hold.
Ask which of the piece's lines the pawn stands on or leaves.
Count again after the pawn move, and compare the two numbers.
items.explain: Counted by the checker: the bishop on d3 attacks 3 squares now and 6 after c5, so the answer is yes. A single pawn move changed a piece's reach without moving the piece.

Now the bishop attacks 3 squares not held by its own pieces.
After c5 the bishop attacks 6 such squares.
